title: Chain inspection: Total receipt
topics: Linked lists, binary trees and search trees
summary: Linked traversal. Add all numbers in the result list.
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
head is the first node of a linked list. In examples, [4, 7] means nodes 4 then 7, linked in that order. [] means no nodes. The runner builds the nodes for you. k is included in the function call, but this task does not use it. You can ignore it.

Step 1: Build the result list
head is the first node of a linked list. A node holds a number in val and a link to the next node in next. Follow next until there are no more nodes. Record each val in order. The list has no loops. An empty list gives an empty result list.

Step 2: Return the answer
Add all numbers in the result list. Return the total. An empty list has a total of 0.

Write your function
Complete chainInspectionTotalReceipt(head, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.
unitIntro: head is the first node of a linked list. A node holds a number in val and a link to the next node in next. Follow next until there are no more nodes. Record each val in order. The list has no loops. An empty list gives an empty result list. Each card first builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.
constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
Linked lists do not loop back to an earlier node. Tree examples list nodes by level; null means a missing child. The runner builds the nodes shown in the examples.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the number of nodes. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
hints: Try a small example by hand. Follow Step 1 and write down its result list.

head is the first node of a linked list. A node holds a number in val and a link to the next node in next. Follow next until there are no more nodes. Record each val in order. The list has no loops. An empty list gives an empty result list. Keep track of the numbers or places you have already checked.
Add all numbers in the result list. Return the total. An empty list has a total of 0. Check what to do if the result list is empty.

cases.explanation: Step 1 gives the result list [7,-3,7,0,12]. Add its numbers to get 23. Return 23.
Step 1 gives the result list [4,4,-2,4]. Add its numbers to get 10. Return 10.
Step 1 gives the result list []. Add its numbers to get 0. Return 0.

overview: The two steps ask different things: first build a list, then return the answer requested. Follow the order, keep repeated values when required, and check the empty case.
